fatal_errors: The proposed elevated-temperature regime conflicts with the target's room-temperature nanoindentation-creep conditions.
It misses interface coherency as the governing variable and therefore does not predict the nonmonotonic optimum at a 16 nm modulation period.

It claims that interfaces suppress diffusion, whereas the target mechanism proposes that pileup-induced amorphization at semicoherent interfaces enables diffusion or interface slip while improving stress redistribution.
The homogeneous-alloy baseline does not reconstruct the key comparison among coherent, semicoherent, and grain-boundary-dominated multilayers.
The cited γ/γ′ high-entropy superalloy evidence concerns a materially different interface architecture and does not directly support the proposed multilayer-coating mechanism.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses creep resistance in HEA coatings and offers a testable, composition-matched comparison with useful measurements. Its generic claim that interfaces impede dislocations and produce pileups overlaps part of the target mechanism. However, it does not reconstruct the decisive modulation-period experiment, the coherent-to-semicoherent-to-grain-boundary transition, the 16 nm optimum, or the stress-exponent signature of a mechanism transition. Its temperature boundary and diffusion claim run counter to the target. Varying spacing and interfacial chemistry simultaneously also confounds the proposed test. E1 and E2 provide limited analogical support from γ/γ′ high-entropy superalloys, while E3 is largely tangential; none establishes the claimed behavior in FCC/BCC Al-Cr-Fe-Ni multilayers.
